gapFill.title: Fill in the gaps
gapFill.subtitle: Type the, or — (dash) when no article is needed. Twenty original sentences.

questions.before: I bought a cake and a pie.
questions.explain: Second mention: we already know which cake, so ‘the’.

questions.before: We met a girl and her dog.
questions.explain: Second mention of ‘dog’: ‘the dog’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
We both know which window: ‘the window’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
A specific film we both know: ‘the film’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
There’s only one sun: ‘the sun’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
There’s only one internet: ‘the internet’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
Superlatives take ‘the’: ‘the best’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
Superlative: ‘the highest’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
Ordinals take ‘the’: ‘the first time’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
Musical instruments: ‘play the drums’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
Places in town we use: ‘the bank’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.after: woman in the blue dress is my aunt.
questions.explain: ‘In the blue dress’ tells us which woman: ‘the’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
Films in general (plural): no ‘the’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
Cats in general: no ‘the’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
Music in general (uncountable): no ‘the’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
Sports take no article: ‘play basketball’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
Meals take no article: ‘have lunch’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
Languages take no article: ‘speak Japanese’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
School subjects take no article. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.after: coffee in this café is amazing.
questions.explain: ‘In this café’ makes it specific: ‘the coffee’. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

wordOrder.title: Put it in order
wordOrder.subtitle: Tap the words to build each sentence — 20 examples with the (and without it).

matching.title: Why the?
matching.subtitle: Tap a sentence, then tap the reason for the (or no article).

pairs.left: I saw a cat. The cat was black.
She’s the tallest in the class.
We bought a sofa. The sofa is green.
The earth goes round the sun.
It’s the worst film I’ve seen.
We rented a car. The car broke down.
I wrote a poem. The poem is short.

timedMC.title: Beat the clock
timedMC.subtitle: 15 seconds per question. Do we know which one? → the. In general, sports, meals, languages → no article.

questions.text: Can you turn off        TV? I’m trying to sleep.
wrongReasons: ‘A TV’ means any TV, but we mean the one in the room.
A singular countable noun needs an article.
‘TV’ starts with a consonant sound, and it’s specific anyway.
questions.explain: We both know which TV: the TV. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: moon looks huge tonight.
wrongReasons: ‘Moon’ is singular and countable: it needs an article.
‘Moon’ starts with a consonant sound, and it’s unique.
questions.explain: Only one exists: the moon. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: That’s        funniest joke I’ve ever heard!
questions.explain: Superlative: the funniest. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: This is        third time he’s been late this week!
questions.explain: Ordinals: the first, the second, the third. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: Can you play        guitar?
wrongReasons: ‘Play a guitar’ is unusual for the skill.
questions.explain: Instruments: play the guitar. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: They play        tennis every weekend.
wrongReasons: Sports take no article. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
questions.explain: Sports: play tennis. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: elephants are very intelligent animals.
questions.explain: Elephants in general: no article. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: I think        health is more important than money.
wrongReasons: ‘The health’ means a specific person’s health.
questions.explain: Uncountable in general: no article. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: people next door are really noisy.
wrongReasons: ‘Next door’ makes them specific: we need ‘the’.
‘Some people next door’ sounds odd: we know who.
questions.explain: ‘Next door’ tells us which people: the. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: I ordered a soup and a salad.        soup was cold.
wrongReasons: A singular noun needs an article.
questions.explain: Second mention: the soup. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: We had        dinner at a Thai restaurant.
wrongReasons: ‘Had the dinner’ is only for a specific dinner.
‘Had a dinner’ is unusual for a normal meal.
questions.explain: Meals: have dinner. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: I’m going to        post office to send a parcel.
wrongReasons: We usually say ‘the post office’ for the one we use.
A singular noun needs an article.
questions.explain: Places in town: the post office. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: Do you speak        Italian?
questions.explain: Languages: speak Italian. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: Global warming is a danger to        planet.
wrongReasons: ‘A planet’ is any planet; we mean ours.
A singular noun needs an article.
questions.explain: Our planet, the one we know: the planet. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: Who is        oldest person in your family?
questions.explain: Superlative: the oldest. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: I’m not very good at        physics.
questions.explain: Subjects: physics, maths, history. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: Which sentence is correct?
choices: I play a piano every day.
wrongReasons: ‘A piano’ isn’t used for the skill.
questions.explain: Instruments take ‘the’; sports don’t. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explain: In general: no article. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: Where did you put        keys? I can’t find them.
wrongReasons: We mean specific keys we both know.
questions.explain: Specific, known keys: the keys. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.

questions.text: My little brother is afraid of        spiders.
questions.explain: Plural in general: no article. Ask “Which one?” — if the listener knows, use the; in general, no article.
